orderConfirmation throws on an invalid email inside createOrder's try after the order is already saved, so the client gets a 500 for an order that was placed; the retry logic also does not wait after the final attempt and mixes throttle/soft-bounce delay state.

sendWithRetry's cyclomatic complexity rose from 3 to 11, with tangled soft-bounce branches (an attempt-conditional branch followed by an unconditional return) and shared delay state that are hard to follow.

The customer name (and sku) is still interpolated unescaped into invoice HTML, flagged in two prior window reviews and still unfixed (an HTML injection vulnerability), while this window added more rows to the same function.

The sale price is the fractional product of priceCents and (1 - pct/100), which is never rounded to whole cents, so unit prices can be non-integer cents.
No tests accompany the new duplicate-registration check, the cancellation window, pagination, or the retry/back-off behaviour.
The generic pagination helper `page` is placed in repo.ts as a free function and imported by the service, mixing a utility into the repository module.

findings.description: Per-line invoice tax is computed on the undiscounted line amount, while order.taxCents is computed on subtotal minus discount, so the line taxes do not add up to the tax total shown on the same invoice whenever a coupon is used.

orderConfirmation can throw (invalid email) after the order is already saved, so the handler returns a 500 for an order that was actually created; the confirmation mail is not isolated from order success.
Business-day counts now skip public holidays, but estimateDelivery only skips weekends, so delivery estimates and business-day counts disagree about what a business day is.

shippingCost has grown into a stack of overlapping region branches, oversize, small-order and weight-tier surcharges that all add up, with hard-coded per-region numbers and a separate REGION_MULTIPLIER in config applied on top, making the pricing hard to reason about and easy to double-charge.

findings.description: shippingCost grew from complexity 2 to 14 with stacked region, oversize, small-order and weight-tier branches plus inline magic numbers (900, 400, 2400, 1200, 3000, 1500, 4000, 2000).

Region surcharges are added and then the whole total is multiplied by REGION_MULTIPLIER, so eu/intl are charged the regional uplift twice (flat surcharges and 1.6x/2.4x multiplier); the oversize surcharge is also compounded.

Weight tier thresholds overlap with the existing per-kg price and the small-order surcharge condition 'kg === 0' is applied for zero-weight parcels regardless of subtotal, while tiers are only checked by kg so the oversize (>30kg) surcharge stacks with the 25kg and 50kg tier surcharges.

cancel now rejects any order older than 24h, which changes the existing cancel contract (orders older than a day can never be cancelled); more importantly the history uses unsorted insertion order and paging is unbounded on the route, but the main defect is that history route does not verify the customer exists or authorise access to req.params.id.
GET /customers/:id/orders returns any customer's order history for an arbitrary id without any authentication or ownership check.
orderConfirmation throws on an invalid stored email after the order has already been saved, so the catch returns a 500 error for an order that was actually placed, and the send result is ignored.

Holiday and same-day handling is inconsistent: the reversed range recursion negates counts, HOLIDAYS is a hard-coded 2026-only list that silently stops excluding holidays after the year, and estimateDelivery does not skip holidays, so invoice and delivery business-day logic disagree.
Sale price product.priceCents * (1 - salePercent/100) yields fractional cents (e.g. 2199*0.8=1759.2) that are never rounded, flowing into integer-cent totals.
legacyInvoiceNumber is a new export that nothing consumes.
Email validity is checked in registration and again in orderConfirmation, which can never fail for registered customers and just adds a throw path.
Large behavioural changes to shipping surcharges, business-day counting and the cancellation window are made with no tests.
dates.ts was patched in five separate commits for successive business-day fixes in one function, indicating an unsettled design.
The cancel status check, flagged in an earlier review as guarded by review only, was rewritten into canCancel, still with no test guarding it.

findings.description: Free-shipping check was changed from >= to >, so an order of exactly FREE_SHIPPING_MIN_CENTS now pays shipping, contradicting the comment that says 'or more ship free'.

The history endpoint's `cancellable` flag uses a hardcoded 48-hour window while OrderService.canCancel enforces 24 hours, so clients are told orders are cancellable that cancel() will reject; the logic is duplicated instead of reusing canCancel.

orderConfirmation can throw for an invalid customer email after the order has already been saved, so createOrder returns a 500 for an order that was actually placed; the confirmation mail should not fail the request.

The retry logic is convoluted and its delay state leaks across attempts: delayMs persists from a previous throttle/soft-bounce, so the mixed-result sequences use stale or escalating delays. Complexity rose from 3 to 11, with the soft-bounce last-attempt branch duplicating the loop's own termination.
The customer display name (and sku) is still interpolated into invoice HTML unescaped; this was flagged in two prior reviews as review-only with no test and remains unfixed, a recurring XSS issue.

Per-line tax is computed on the undiscounted line amount while order.taxCents is computed on the discounted subtotal, so the invoice's tax column does not sum to the stated tax total when a coupon is applied; per-line rounding also drifts.
The sale price returns a fractional number of cents (priceCents * (1 - pct/100) is not rounded), which flows into unitCents and totals that are supposed to be integer cents.
The duplicate-email check happens before the firstName validation, and the find-then-save is a linear scan over all customers, which is O(n) per registration.

Behaviour added in the window (cancellation window, pagination, retry/backoff, regional shipping and tax, markup in invoices) has no accompanying tests, which is how the 24h/48h mismatch and the boundary change went unnoticed.

The generic pagination helper `page` is placed in the repo module and imported by the service, and the history endpoint is missing a customer-existence check, so an unknown customer id returns 200 with an empty list rather than 404.
The cancel error message was merged into a single 'can no longer be cancelled' message, losing the distinction between a non-placed status and an expired window.

findings.description: The history route computes `cancellable` with a hard-coded 48-hour window while OrderService.canCancel enforces 24 hours, so clients are told orders are cancellable that cancel() will reject; the logic is duplicated instead of reusing canCancel.
Free-shipping check changed from >= to > while the comment still says 'or more', so an order exactly at FREE_SHIPPING_MIN_CENTS now pays shipping.

orderConfirmation throws on an invalid email inside createOrder after the order was already saved, so the client gets a 500 for an order that was actually placed; the email is also validated at registration, so the check is redundant.

Complexity rose from 3 to 11 with tangled delay state: soft-bounce and throttle branches are interleaved, a throttle delay carries over into later attempts, and the soft-bounce-on-last-attempt branch duplicates the loop's exit.

The doc comment says it tries up to MAX_SEND_ATTEMPTS, but a 'rejected' result stops after the first attempt and the retry semantics are not documented; after a soft bounce followed by a throttle the backoff doubles from the soft-bounce delay.
Customer name (and sku) is still interpolated into invoice HTML unescaped, flagged in two earlier reviews as review-only with no test, and this window added another raw row without fixing it.
Markup in the customer name is injected into the HTML invoice (stored XSS), since displayName is not escaped.

Per-line tax is recomputed from the undiscounted line amount while order.taxCents is computed on the discounted subtotal, so line taxes do not sum to the order tax shown when a coupon is applied; rounding per line also diverges.
Sale price priceCents * (1 - percent/100) is not rounded to integer cents (e.g. 4999*0.8 = 3999.2), producing fractional-cent unit prices that flow into totals.

The history route is unauthenticated and does not check the customer exists, returning orders for any id; it also mixes in the order repo helper `page` exported from the repo module as a free function.
Tax rates per region live in pricing.ts while shipping region multipliers live in config.ts, and config.ts now imports a type from orders, splitting region-based constants across modules.
New behaviours (duplicate email rejection, retry/backoff, cancellation window) have no tests in the window.
Duplicate check is a linear scan over all customers and the check-then-save is not atomic; it also runs before the firstName validation, and the lowercase invariant is only by convention.

findings.description: page() is documented as 1-based but computes start = pageNumber * size, so page 1 skips the first 25 orders and the first page of history is never returned.

findById now throws NotFoundError instead of returning null, but its doc comment, CustomerService.find (documented to return null) and callers in routes.ts (createOrder 'unknown customer' 400 and invoice 409 null checks) still assume null, so unknown customers now yield 404 or an unhandled throw (invoice has no try/catch) and the null branches are dead.
Invoice lineTax duplicates regional tax logic from pricing.TAX_RATES with a different EU rate (0.21 vs 0.2) and Math.floor vs roundCents, so per-line taxes disagree with the order's taxCents.

orderConfirmation throws on an invalid email after the order has already been placed and saved, so createOrder returns an error status for an order that exists; the confirmation also is sent before the response and its result is ignored.
Sale price is priceCents * (1 - percent/100), which yields fractional cents (e.g. 4999*0.8=3999.2) that are not rounded and flow into totals and integer-cent formatting.

Free-shipping threshold ignores the region, so intl and EU orders over the minimum ship free despite the new regional multipliers; also the free-shipping subtotal logic is unchanged from before regional rates.
No tests accompany pagination, cancellation window, regional tax/shipping, or duplicate-registration changes, which is how the off-by-one pagination and inconsistent tax rates went unnoticed.
Invoice rows now have a tax column but no table header, and line.sku is inserted into the HTML unescaped while the customer name is escaped.
Generic pagination helper is placed in the order repo module and imported by the service, and the exported name 'page' collides with the local concept of page number.
orderHistory does not verify the customer exists or handle errors, and does not use try/catch like other handlers.

findings.description: orderConfirmation divides totalCents by 100 and passes dollars to formatMoney, which expects cents, so the email shows a total 100x too small (e.g. $0.50 instead of $50.00).

The sale is extended by a full day (saleEndsAt + DAY_MS) though saleEndsAt is documented as the instant the sale ends, so the sale runs a day past its end; a product with a past saleEndsAt and salePercent 0 or null is fine but the semantics are inconsistent with the Product doc.

orderConfirmation can throw after the order has been saved, so createOrder returns a 500 for an order that was actually placed (the client may retry and duplicate it); the confirmation email should not fail the request.

cancel now also enforces the 24-hour window, but the route and error message give no distinction, and orderHistory's page is computed from the internal list; more importantly the window check changes cancel behavior beyond the stated status-only rule, with no test coverage.
Per-line tax is rounded individually while order.taxCents is computed on the discounted subtotal, so line taxes ignore the coupon discount and do not sum to the order's tax shown on the invoice.
orderHistory returns any customer's orders by id with no existence check or authorization, and does not handle an unknown customer.
listByCustomer still returns the repository's internal array by reference, flagged in two earlier reviews and guarded only by review; the new history path now feeds it onward.
New behaviors (cancellation window, sale boundary and clamping, duplicate registration, regional shipping and tax, pagination) have no tests.
ordersToCsv is exported but never used, and it does not escape fields.

products.ts was changed in 6 commits in one window, with successive rounding/clamp fixes (round to cents, half away from zero, clamp, min one cent) layered onto priceFor and a redundant roundCents path.
DAY_MS is redefined in products.ts duplicating the constant in util/dates.ts, and CANCEL_WINDOW_MS is another inline day constant.
The pagination helper lives in repo.ts as a free function but is only used by the service, and shippingCost uses Math.round instead of roundCents, inconsistent rounding helpers.
Tax rates are split between config (TAX_RATE) and a local TAX_RATES table in pricing, and config.ts now imports types from orders, creating a config-to-domain dependency.

orderHistory does not check that the customer exists or handle errors, so an unknown customer id returns an empty 200 instead of a 404.
None of the new behaviour (surcharge combinations, holiday and reversed-range business days, the 24h cancel window) has tests in the window; the only guard is review.
